questions.q:
With reference to the Index of Services Production launched by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It is a nominal turnover index that measures changes in the value of services sold.
2. Its base year is 2024-25.
3. It relies mainly on GST data and covers both formal and informal services.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. The index is a volume index of real output, with price effects removed using WPI, sector-specific CPI or general CPI deflators, so statement 1 is wrong. It draws mainly on GSTR-1 data and covers formal, largely GST-registered services, leaving informal services out. The first trial index, for April 2026, came out on 14 July 2026.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 39; Shankar IAS pp. 89-90

questions.q: The Index of Services Production is compiled as a fixed-weight Laspeyres volume index in which the weight of each service sector is its share in
questions.e: Weights come from each sector's share in Gross Value Added, as in the industrial index. The index covers 19 sub-sectors, about 60 per cent of services, and will be released on the 29th of each month with a lag of about 60 days. A technical advisory committee chaired by Debjani Ghosh of NITI Aayog guided its design.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 39; Shankar IAS p. 90

questions.q:
Which of the following are excluded from the coverage of the Index of Services Production?
1. Public administration and defence
2. Telecommunications
3. Central banking
4. Gambling and betting
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Non-market, government-dominated, informal or hard-to-measure activities are left out: public administration and defence, government health and education, central banking, household and personal services, and gambling and betting. Telecommunications is covered, along with trade, transport, banking, insurance, IT and hotels. Private health and education will be added when the services enterprise survey gives enough data.

questions.q:
With reference to the revised Index of Core Industries with base year 2022-23, consider the following statements:
1. Iron ore has been added as a ninth core industry.
2. Refinery products now carry the largest weight in the index.
3. The combined weight of core industries in the Index of Industrial Production has risen.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct; iron ore is now the ninth core industry. The core share in the industrial index fell from 40.27 to 32.88 per cent. Electricity, at about 30.9, now has the largest weight, overtaking refinery products at about 22.6. Steel is now measured by gross output. Remember the difference between the ICI, the IIP and the new Index of Services Production.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The Index of Core Industries is used as a lead indicator for the Index of Industrial Production.
Statement-II: Both indices are compiled and released by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct and Statement-II is incorrect. The core index is released by the Office of the Economic Adviser in DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, while the industrial index is compiled by the statistics ministry. With the new series, GDP, WPI, the industrial index and the core index now share 2022-23 as a common base year.

questions.q:
With reference to the SDG National Indicator Framework Progress Report, 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It was released by NITI Aayog.
2. It puts social protection coverage in India at 65.3 per cent in 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 2 is correct. The report is from the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, which developed the framework with ministries, NITI Aayog and UN agencies. Its 65.3 per cent social-protection figure differs from the ILO's 68.4 per cent. It also reports the national unemployment rate falling to 3.1 per cent in 2025 and municipal waste processing rising to 82.2 per cent.

questions.q:
With reference to the Periodic Labour Force Survey 2025, consider the following statements:
1. The labour force participation rate of persons aged 15 and above rose above 50 per cent.
2. The female labour force participation rate was 27.2 per cent.
3. The unemployment rate on usual status was lower than in 2017-18.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three statements are correct. Overall participation was 52.4 per cent, up from 47.7 per cent in 2017-18; female participation rose by 7.4 points to 27.2 per cent; and unemployment fell from 7.9 to 4.9 per cent. About 69 per cent of women outside the labour force cite domestic duties, which is why care work features in policy proposals.

questions.q: The National Statistics Office was formed in 2019 by merging the
o: Directorate of Economics and Statistics and the Labour Bureau
Labour Bureau and the Central Statistics Office
National Sample Survey Office and the Registrar General of India
Central Statistics Office and the National Sample Survey Office
questions.e: The merged office under the statistics ministry compiles GDP, the industrial index and CPI and runs large surveys such as the labour force survey, started in 2017, and the survey of unincorporated enterprises. In 2026 the latter gave the first city-level picture for India's 46 million-plus cities, which account for 21 per cent of the sector's value added.

questions.q:
With reference to the Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises 2025, consider the following statements:
1. It covers unincorporated non-agricultural enterprises in manufacturing, trade and services but excludes construction.
2. Gross value added per worker in million-plus cities was lower than in other urban areas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. In million-plus cities, value added per worker was about Rs 2.11 lakh against Rs 1.80 lakh in other urban areas, with Pimpri Chinchwad, Greater Hyderabad, Delhi and Faridabad leading. In Surat, Vadodara and Pune women owned over 40 per cent of proprietary establishments.

questions.q: The 'U-shaped' relationship between economic development and women's labour force participation, used to explain the long decline in India's female participation until 2018-19, is associated with
questions.e: Goldin's hypothesis holds that female participation first falls as economies move out of agriculture and household incomes rise, and later rises as education and non-farm jobs expand. In India, mechanisation and the shift away from farming pushed rural women out between 2004-05 and 2012. Female worker-population ratio is still below 30 per cent, and only 15 per cent in Bihar.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Much of the rise in women's employment in India after 2020 has been described as distress-driven.
Statement-II: The COVID-19 shock and return migration pushed many women into subsistence farming and unpaid family work.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct and the second explains the first. The growth was concentrated among older, less educated women re-entering agriculture and allied work, not in better-paid non-farm jobs. Labour-intensive sectors such as textiles and food processing lost jobs between 2013 and 2019, and women's manufacturing employment regained its 2004 level only in 2022.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Scheme : Ministry or department
1. WISE-KIRAN : Department of Science and Technology
2. Stand-Up India : Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
3. NAVYA : Ministry of Commerce and Industry
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Only pair 1 is correct. Stand-Up India, offering loans of Rs 10 lakh to Rs 1 crore to SC, ST and women entrepreneurs, is run by the Department of Financial Services in the Ministry of Finance. NAVYA trains adolescent girls aged 16 to 18 and is run by the Ministries of Women and Child Development and of Skill Development.

questions.q: Which State, with about 5 to 6 per cent of India's population, accounts for over 40 per cent of India's women factory workers?
questions.e: Tamil Nadu's textile and garment hubs at Tiruppur and Coimbatore, footwear clusters, electronics assembly around Sriperumbudur and automobile industry, combined with higher female literacy, safer transport and hostels, explain the figure. Replicating such clusters in Hindi-belt States is proposed to raise women's employment.

questions.q:
With reference to Gen Z employment in India, consider the following statements:
1. Gen Z is defined as those born between 1997 and 2012.
2. The unemployment rate among Gen Z is lower than among Millennials.
3. Graduate unemployment among young women is higher than among young men.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; graduate unemployment is about 36.9 per cent for young women against 29 per cent for young men. Gen Z unemployment, about 11.9 per cent, far exceeds the Millennial rate of about 2 per cent, so statement 2 is wrong. Nearly 80 per cent of employed Gen Z lack a written contract or social protection.

questions.q:
With reference to the Employees' Provident Fund Scheme, 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It replaces the Employees' Provident Fund Scheme, 1952, as part of implementing the Code on Social Security, 2020.
2. Purpose-wise partial withdrawals have been grouped into three categories: illness; education and marriage; and housing.
3. The government may defer contributions for up to three months during a pandemic or national disaster.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three statements are correct. New Employees' Pension and Deposit-Linked Insurance schemes of 2026 also replace the 1995 and 1976 schemes. Contributions stay at 12 per cent each, or 10 per cent for notified establishments. VISHWAS 2026 gives six months to settle disputes over defaults before 14 June 2024, and AMNESTY 2026 regularises exemptions of eligible PF trusts.

questions.q:
With reference to ILO Convention No. 193 on decent work in the platform economy, consider the following statements:
1. India voted in favour of the Convention.
2. It covers only location-based platform workers such as delivery and ride-hailing workers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither statement is correct. India abstained when the Convention was adopted at the 114th International Labour Conference in Geneva. It covers all platform workers, online and location-based, formal and informal, and provides for correct classification, timely pay, freedom of association, data protection, transparency in algorithmic decisions with a right to human review, and safeguards for migrant workers.

questions.q:
With reference to India's sovereign credit ratings, consider the following statements:
1. S&P upgraded India to BBB in August 2025, its first upgrade of India in 18 years.
2. Credit rating agencies in India are regulated by SEBI.
3. CareEdge is the first global sovereign rating agency headquartered in India.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three statements are correct. Rating agencies are regulated by SEBI under its 1999 regulations framed under the SEBI Act, 1992; the RBI only accredits agencies whose ratings banks may use for capital purposes. Other recent upgrades were by Moody's to Baa2 in 2017, Morningstar DBRS to BBB in May 2025 and R&I of Japan. India argues ratings understate its willingness to repay.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 43; Shankar IAS pp. 102-103

questions.q: 'Rating shopping', one of the criticisms of credit rating agencies, refers to the practice of
o: issuers approaching several agencies and disclosing only the most favourable rating
agencies lowering ratings to attract more clients
investors buying ratings from unregistered agencies
questions.e: Rating shopping arises from the issuer-pays model, in which the entity being rated pays the agency, creating a conflict of interest. Other criticisms are opaque methods, weak accountability and alleged bias against emerging economies. Suggested reforms include neutral fee allocation, detailed disclosure of methods, analyst rotation and risk-based inspections by SEBI.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: India's sovereign rating has never been upgraded by S&P.
Statement-II: India did not default on its external debt even during the balance of payments crisis of 1991.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct. S&P upgraded India to BBB in August 2025, its first upgrade in 18 years. India did not default even in 1991, and argues that ratings understate its willingness to repay, since agencies judge ability from growth, deficits and reserves and willingness partly from governance indicators.

questions.q:
With reference to polymer banknotes, consider the following statements:
1. They are printed on a substrate of biaxially oriented polypropylene.
2. They were first introduced by Australia in 1988.
3. The RBI's polymer note field trial of 2026 is its first attempt to introduce such notes.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; over 50 countries now use polymer notes. Statement 3 is wrong: the RBI first proposed polymer Rs 10 notes in 2009, with field trials planned in five cities from Shimla to Kochi, but the plan was dropped over technical and procurement problems. Polymer notes last two to six times longer than cotton-paper notes.

questions.q:
With reference to the RBI's 2026 directions on 'Specified Non-Financial Assets', consider the following statements:
1. These are immovable properties that banks acquire from defaulting borrowers in settlement of loans.
2. A bank may sell such an asset back to the original borrower at a discount.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. Banks may acquire such property only after the loan becomes a non-performing asset, overdue for more than 90 days, and only through full or partial settlement. Disposal is mainly by public auction on SARFAESI principles, and resale to the original borrower or related parties is barred.

questions.q: The Coal Blocks Allocation (Amendment) Rules, 2026 allow allottees to furnish an 'Insurance Surety Bond' in place of a Performance Bank Guarantee. The main difference between the two is that
o: a surety bond covers only environmental damage, while a bank guarantee covers production targets
a surety bond is issued by an insurance company, while a bank guarantee is issued by a bank
a surety bond is issued by the Coal Controller, while a bank guarantee is issued by the RBI
a surety bond is non-enforceable, while a bank guarantee is enforceable
questions.e: Both instruments compensate the government if the allottee defaults on its obligations; they differ in who issues them. Surety bonds free up bank credit lines that guarantees would otherwise lock up. The change applies to blocks allocated under the MMDR Act, 1957, with an extension proposed to the Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act, 2015.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The CBDT's 2026 guidelines on crypto-asset reporting legalise and regulate trading in crypto-assets in India.
Statement-II: The guidelines align crypto tax reporting with the OECD's Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework for automatic exchange of information.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is incorrect and Statement-II is correct. The guidelines only prescribe tax reporting: exchanges must identify users and report transactions annually, and the data are exchanged automatically with users' tax jurisdictions. They do not legalise or regulate crypto-assets. Crypto had escaped the earlier Common Reporting Standard because it can be held outside the financial system.

questions.q:
With reference to NITI Aayog's Investment Friendliness Index, consider the following statements:
1. It was announced in the Union Budget 2025-26.
2. Infrastructure carries the highest weight among its eight pillars.
3. Maharashtra topped the index.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; infrastructure carries 25 per cent, followed by business climate at 20 per cent. Gujarat topped with 56.6, followed by Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Goa and Odisha, so statement 3 is wrong. The index uses 84 indicators to promote competitive and cooperative federalism among States.

questions.q:
With reference to UNCTAD's World Investment Report 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Global FDI rose to about 1.6 trillion dollars in 2025.
2. FDI growth in developing economies was faster than in developed economies.
3. India's rank among recipients of inward FDI improved to 11th.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Developed economies saw growth of 11 per cent against 2 per cent for developing ones, so statement 2 is wrong; the top 20 hosts took over 80 per cent of inflows. Greenfield investment was led by AI infrastructure, data centres and semiconductors. India's outward FDI rank rose from 20th to 18th.

questions.q: The 'World Intangible Investment Report', which found in 2026 that India recorded the fastest growth in intangible investment among the 15 largest economies, is published by
o: the World Economic Forum and INSEAD
questions.e: WIPO and Italy's Luiss Business School publish it annually. Intangible investment, in R&D, software, databases, brands, design and organisational know-how, has grown over three times faster than tangible investment since 2008. The US leads in total and Sweden in intensity. India's fastest-growing category was software and databases.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: In 2026 the government permitted FDI in the inventory-based model of e-commerce only for exports of domestically manufactured goods.
Statement-II: Limiting the relaxation to exports protects the domestic market from predatory pricing by foreign-funded platforms.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are correct and the second explains the restriction in the first. Earlier, FDI was allowed only in B2B e-commerce and the marketplace model; inventory-based retail to Indian consumers remains closed. The opening helps MSMEs export through large platforms that can handle testing, labelling and traceability rules such as the EU Digital Product Passport.

questions.q:
With reference to the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund, consider the following statements:
1. It was set up in 2015 as a SEBI-registered Category II Alternative Investment Fund.
2. The Government of India holds a majority stake of 51 per cent in each fund it manages.
3. Its Governing Council is chaired by the Union Finance Minister.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The government holds 49 per cent in each NIIF-managed fund, which keeps it a minority investor, so statement 2 is wrong. In 2026 the Cabinet approved a further Rs 30,000 crore to anchor Infrastructure Fund II for transport, energy, digital and urban infrastructure and e-mobility.

questions.q:
With reference to the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies, which India accepted in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It was adopted at the 13th Ministerial Conference in Abu Dhabi in 2024.
2. It prohibits subsidies to aquaculture and inland fisheries.
3. It is the first multilateral WTO agreement with an environmental sustainability objective.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 3 is correct. The agreement was adopted at MC12 in Geneva in 2022 and entered into force in September 2025; MC13 in Abu Dhabi failed to agree on the second phase on overcapacity. Aquaculture and inland fisheries are outside its scope, which protects India's farmed-shrimp exports. It bars subsidies for illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing and for overfished stocks.

questions.q: In the second phase of WTO fisheries negotiations, India is seeking
o: a ban on all fuel subsidies to fishers
removal of the peace clause for developing countries
inclusion of aquaculture within the subsidy disciplines
a 25-year transition period for developing countries and a permanent carve-out for small-scale and artisanal fishers
questions.e: India also wants stricter disciplines on distant-water industrial fleets, whose large subsidies distort competition with its mostly small-scale fishers. The current agreement already gives developing countries a two-year peace clause for certain subsidies within their EEZs, and a voluntary WTO Fish Fund helps them align their laws.

questions.q:
With reference to the modernisation of the public distribution system, consider the following statements:
1. One Nation One Ration Card portability is available in all 36 States and Union Territories.
2. Coverage under the National Food Security Act is still capped on the basis of Census 2011 population.
3. 'Anna Chakra' is a mobile app for beneficiaries to check their entitlements.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; the cap of 81.35 crore leaves a shortfall of about 79 lakh. Anna Chakra is a supply-chain route-optimisation tool, so statement 3 is wrong; the beneficiary apps are Mera Ration and Anna Mitra. A parliamentary committee in 2026 also noted 2.91 crore red-flagged beneficiaries and 6.77 crore cards removed since 2013.

questions.q:
With reference to the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana, consider the following statements:
1. Its National Steering Committee is chaired by the Prime Minister.
2. 'Per Drop More Crop' is implemented by the Ministry of Jal Shakti.
3. Irrigation potential of over 24 million hectares has been created or restored under it.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Per Drop More Crop, the micro-irrigation component, is run by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare; the Jal Shakti ministry runs the Accelerated Irrigation Benefits Programme and Har Khet Ko Pani, and the Department of Land Resources runs watershed development. The scheme, launched on 1 July 2015, completed ten years in 2026.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Irrigation project : State
1. Saryu Nahar National Project : Uttar Pradesh
2. Renukaji Dam : Uttarakhand
3. Lakhwar Multipurpose Project : Himachal Pradesh
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Only pair 1 is correct; the Saryu canal, begun in 1978, was completed after being brought under PMKSY and benefits about 29 lakh farmers. The other two are swapped: Renukaji is in Himachal Pradesh and Lakhwar in Uttarakhand. Both are Yamuna-basin storage projects funded 90 per cent by the Centre and benefiting six States.

questions.q:
With reference to the National Investment Policy for Urea, 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It offers new gas-based urea plants a return on equity within a band of 12 to 16 per cent.
2. It aims at 8 to 9 new gas-based plants with a combined capacity of about 10 million tonnes.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both statements are correct. The policy, which replaces the New Investment Policy of 2012, separates fixed and variable costs and converts fixed costs into rupees after four years to reduce exchange-rate risk. India is the world's largest urea importer, with imports of about 103.5 lakh tonnes in 2025-26, nearly double the year before.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 48-49; Shankar IAS pp. 86-87

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: India is the world's largest consumer of urea.
Statement-II: India is the world's largest importer of urea.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is incorrect and Statement-II is correct. India is only the second-largest consumer but the largest importer, because domestic output of about 306 lakh tonnes falls short of demand of about 387 lakh tonnes. China supplied over 22 per cent of imports in early 2026, followed by Russia and the Gulf. Urea sells at Rs 266.50 per 45-kg bag against a global cost of over Rs 4,100.
questions.s: Shankar IAS p. 88; Vision IAS p. 49

questions.q: Which one of the following is not an initiative to improve fertiliser-use efficiency or reduce chemical fertiliser use?
questions.e: Urea is not covered by the Nutrient Based Subsidy scheme; it is sold at a fixed maximum retail price, and that cheapness encourages overuse and nutrient imbalance. Neem coating slows nitrogen loss and prevents diversion, PM-PRANAM rewards States that reduce chemical fertiliser use, and IFFCO's nano urea is a liquid alternative. Crops use only 30 to 35 per cent of applied nitrogen.
questions.s: Shankar IAS p. 89; Vision IAS p. 49

questions.q:
With reference to tea cultivation in India, consider the following statements:
1. Tea requires alkaline soil with a pH of about 7.5 to 8.5.
2. Tea grows best on flat land where water collects around the roots.
3. Kerala produces more than half of India's tea.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: None of the statements is correct. Tea needs acidic soil with a pH of about 4.5 to 5.5 and cannot tolerate waterlogging, so it is grown on slopes or well-drained soils. Assam produces more than half of India's tea. It needs 20 to 30 degrees Celsius, 150 to 300 cm of well-distributed rain and at least five hours of sunshine.

questions.q:
Indian tea companies faced falling realisations in 2025-26. Which of the following were cited as causes?
1. Cheaper imports from Nepal and Kenya
2. Heatwaves that increased pest attacks and lowered quality
3. A temporary shortage of LPG linked to the West Asia conflict
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: All three were cited, along with four to five quarters of falling prices and a shift by consumers to cheaper loose tea. Large companies have responded by diversifying: Tata's foods and beverages businesses out-earned tea and coffee for the first time, and Goodricke moved into dairy and solar energy. An expected El Nino in late 2026 could hit output.

questions.q:
With reference to the Codex Alimentarius Commission, consider the following statements:
1. It was set up jointly by the FAO and the WHO in 1963.
2. Its standards are legally binding on all member countries.
3. The Codex Committee on Spices and Culinary Herbs was set up at India's initiative, with the Spices Board as its secretariat.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Codex standards are voluntary, though the WTO's SPS Agreement treats them as the international benchmark for food safety, so statement 2 is wrong. At its 49th session in Geneva in 2026, the Commission adopted standards for large cardamom, coriander and vanilla, finalised by the spices committee.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Crop : Fact
1. Large cardamom : Native to the North-Eastern Himalaya; Sikkim is the largest producer
2. Coriander : Grown in India as a kharif crop; Kerala is the largest producer
3. Vanilla : India is a net importer
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 3 are correct. Coriander, native to the Mediterranean, is grown in India as a rabi crop, and Rajasthan is the largest producer followed by Madhya Pradesh. India is the largest producer and exporter of large cardamom and of coriander. Vanilla is native to the Atlantic coast from Mexico to Brazil, with Madagascar a leading producer.

questions.q: Lakadong turmeric, promoted under 'Mission Golden Spice', is a GI-tagged variety native to
questions.e: Lakadong turmeric has a very high curcumin content of 7 to 10 per cent. The mission, launched by the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region with an outlay of Rs 175.45 crore, aims to triple the area to about 7,500 ha by 2028-29 and create over 3,000 jobs led by women. Kandhamal and Erode have their own GI-tagged turmeric.

questions.q:
With reference to cooperatives in India, consider the following statements:
1. Part IX-B of the Constitution, on cooperative societies, was inserted by the 97th Amendment in 2011.
2. Cooperative societies are a subject in the Union List.
3. The Ministry of Cooperation was created in 2019.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct; the amendment also made forming cooperatives a fundamental right under Article 19(1)(c) and added Article 43B. Cooperative societies are a State List subject, while multi-State cooperatives fall in the Union List. The Ministry of Cooperation was carved out in July 2021, and on its fifth anniversary the government announced the 'Bharat Taxi' platform.

questions.q: 'Bharat Taxi', launched in the cooperative sector, is
o: India's first community-owned digital mobility platform
a scheme of the Ministry of Road Transport for electric taxis
a government-owned ride-hailing app run by the Railways
a credit scheme for taxi drivers under PM SVANidhi
questions.e: Bharat Taxi is a cooperative alternative to private ride aggregators, in which drivers are members. Other cooperative initiatives include allowing PACS to take up over 25 businesses such as Jan Aushadhi Kendras and fuel outlets, White Revolution 2.0 to raise cooperative milk procurement by 50 per cent by 2028-29, and the National Cooperation Policy 2025.

questions.q:
With reference to SHE-LEAPS and the Lakhpati Didi initiative, consider the following statements:
1. The Lakhpati Didi target was raised from 3 crore to 5 crore women.
2. SHE-LEAPS was developed by NABARD for self-help group bank linkage.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither statement is correct. The target was raised from 3 crore to 6 crore; a Lakhpati Didi is an SHG woman with a sustainable household income of over Rs 1 lakh a year. SHE-LEAPS is a digital platform of the rural development ministry for enterprise creation and performance tracking, not a NABARD bank-linkage tool.

questions.q:
With reference to the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Act, 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Filing of a memorandum or registration is now free and voluntary for all enterprises.
2. Settlements and awards in delayed-payment disputes can be recovered as arrears of land revenue.
3. Use of the Trade Receivables Discounting System has been made mandatory for all central public sector enterprises.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three statements are correct. The Act also allows multiple facilitation councils per State, sets timelines of 90 days for mediation, 30 days to refer to arbitration and 90 days for an award, and replaces criminal fines with graded penalties and a first warning. Invoices discounted on TReDS rose from Rs 40,000 crore in 2022-23 to Rs 3.47 lakh crore in 2025-26.

questions.q: Under the present criteria, a micro enterprise is one with investment in plant and machinery or equipment of up to Rs 2.5 crore and annual turnover of up to
questions.e: Small enterprises go up to Rs 25 crore investment and Rs 100 crore turnover, and medium enterprises up to Rs 125 crore and Rs 500 crore. The 2026 amendment removed fixed thresholds from the Act itself, so the limits can be notified. MSMEs account for about 31 per cent of GDP and 48.58 per cent of exports.

questions.q:
With reference to Semicon India Programme 2.0, consider the following statements:
1. Its outlay is Rs 1,27,500 crore.
2. The India Semiconductor Mission is its nodal agency.
3. States are reimbursed by the Centre for the land and utilities they provide to projects.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. States provide land, power and water without seeking Central reimbursement, so statement 3 is wrong. The scheme has six pillars and ten categories covering design, equipment and materials, fabs, packaging, R&D and talent, with a target of training one lakh additional engineers. Semicon 1.0 of 2021 had an outlay of Rs 76,000 crore.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Semiconductor project or programme : Description
1. SiCSem Pvt Ltd, Odisha : Silicon carbide fab approved under Semicon 1.0
2. DHRUV64 : 64-bit processor developed by C-DAC
3. Semiconductor Laboratory : Located at Bengaluru
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 1 and 2 are correct. The Semiconductor Laboratory is at Mohali, where 56 chips were fabricated under the Chips to Startup programme. Semicon 1.0 approved 12 units, including nine packaging units such as Tata's in Assam. DHRUV64, like the SHAKTI and VIKRAM families, is built on the open RISC-V architecture.

questions.q: 'More-than-Moore', suggested as a strategy for India's semiconductor industry, refers to
o: doubling the number of fabs every two years
gaining performance through 3D integration, chiplets and advanced packaging rather than only shrinking transistor size
importing all advanced chips while focusing on design
using only silicon instead of compound semiconductors
questions.e: Moore's Law described the doubling of transistors on a chip by shrinking them. As shrinking becomes harder and costlier, gains now come from packaging and integration, areas where India's assembly and testing units can compete. India hosts about 20 per cent of the world's chip-design workforce but imports 90 to 95 per cent of the chips it uses.

questions.q:
With reference to the Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme approved in 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It succeeds the PLI scheme for large-scale electronics manufacturing.
2. It offers an additional incentive to Indian brands that invest in design and R&D.
3. Mobile phones became India's largest export product in 2025-26.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: All three statements are correct. The scheme has Rs 62,500 crore for 2026-27 to 2030-31, with incentives of 2.25 to 5 per cent on sales, up to 1.5 per cent more for local sourcing and 3 per cent more for Indian brands. Mobiles rose from India's 153rd export item in 2014-15 to the top. About 70 per cent of the direct workforce are women.

questions.q:
With reference to the Modified UDAN scheme, consider the following statements:
1. It will run for five years from 2026-27 to 2030-31.
2. It provides for 50 modern helipads in hilly, remote and island areas.
3. It is implemented by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: None of the statements is correct. Modified UDAN runs for ten years, 2026-27 to 2035-36, with Rs 28,840 crore to develop 100 airports and 200 helipads in hilly, remote and island areas. UDAN, launched in October 2016 under the National Civil Aviation Policy, belongs to the Ministry of Civil Aviation and is implemented by the Airports Authority of India.

questions.q:
Under the Atmanirbhar Bharat component of the Modified UDAN scheme, which of the following indigenous aircraft are to be procured?
1. HAL Dhruv helicopters
2. HAL Dornier aircraft
3. HAL Tejas aircraft
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: The scheme envisages procuring Dhruv helicopters and Dornier aircraft for regional connectivity. Tejas is a light combat aircraft for the Air Force, not a civil transport. Under UDAN so far, 669 routes have been opened across 95 airports, heliports and water aerodromes, carrying over 1.66 crore passengers.

questions.q:
With reference to India's first hydrogen-powered train, consider the following statements:
1. It runs on the Jind-Sonipat section in Haryana.
2. It uses proton exchange membrane fuel cells, supplied by an Indian company.
3. Its only by-products are water vapour and heat.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; the 89-km route opened on 17 July 2026. The fuel cells are imported from Ballard of Canada, so statement 2 is wrong; Medha Servo Drives of Hyderabad integrated the propulsion. The ten-coach train has two hydrogen driving power cars with 2,400 kW in all, making it among the longest and most powerful hydrogen trainsets.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The hydrogen train between Jind and Sonipat runs on fuel cells alone and carries no batteries.
Statement-II: The batteries store surplus power at low demand and supplement the fuel cells during acceleration.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct. Each power pack pairs a 115 kW fuel cell with a 185 kW lithium iron phosphate battery, which stores surplus power at low demand and supplements the fuel cells during acceleration. Hydrogen is made by electrolysis at a Jind facility.

questions.q: The first country to run commercial hydrogen-powered passenger trains, using Alstom's Coradia iLint, was
questions.e: Germany launched commercial service in 2018 after the train was shown in Berlin in 2016. France, Italy, China, Japan and the United States have pilots or limited services, mostly with two to four coaches. India's ten-coach train was initiated by Northern Railway in 2020-21 at an estimated Rs 136 crore and approved for commercial operation on 22 May 2026.
